LHT's interim exec chairman makes 75 cents per share partial offer
article:
Li Suet Man, interim executive chairman of LHT Holdings, is making a partial offer for 51% of the company at 75 cents each.

Li is making the offer via an entity jointly held by him and his son, Li Ear, with a combined stake of 25.96%.

Capital Management Partners Fund, which owns 18.45% of the shares, has given its irrevocable undertaking to accept the offer.

At 75 cents, the offer is a 1.3% discount to LHT's last traded price of 76 cents on Oct 5.

As at June 30, LHT's net asset value per share was 73.89 cents, down from 99.71 cent as at Dec 31 2025.

For its 1HFY2026 ended June, LHT reported a loss of $493,000, from earnings of $1.34 million in the year earlier. Revenue in the same period was down 21.1% yo $11.4 million.

See also: Zheneng Jinjiang Environment to be taken private with offer of 70 cents per share

LHT, which makes wooden pallets and other related products, was incorporated in 1980 and listed in 1999.

The Lis want to gain "statutory" control of the company so as to streamline decision-making and improve operational efficiencies.

The partial offer, reads the SGX filing, is also "an opportunity" for other shareholders to realise part of their investment in the company, while continuing to participate in LHT's future performance, which will remain listed.
